subject: Privatenet deployment screening — PrivateLink preference & IP allowlist next steps
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@netfin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Privatenet deployment screening — PrivateLink preference & IP allowlist next steps

Thanks again for taking time today, Alicia — quick recap and the immediate asks so we can keep momentum toward the pilot.

Key points from our call:
- NetFin goal: run customer-facing LLM inference inside your VPC to satisfy data residency and egress control.
- Preference stated: PrivateLink endpoint (customer-managed interface) rather than full VPC peering; reason: avoid cross-account routing and simplify firewall rules.
- Requirements we noted: static egress IPs for outbound requests, ability to accept inbound connections from our PrivateLink endpoint(s), SOC 2 evidence to be delivered to your security team.

Immediate asks for your team:
1) Confirm that PrivateLink is preferred and peering is not an option.
2) Provide list of IPs/subnets that must be added to your allowlist for initial pilot (or confirm that a single ALB-private static egress range is acceptable).
3) Share contact for NetFin NetOps (name + calendar link) so we can schedule a 30–45m technical walk.
4) Any procurement timing constraints or PO cadence we should plan against?

Attachments: network-intake-form.pdf (please fill high-level network answers), redwood-privatelink-architecture.png (diagram).

Proposed next steps from our side:
- Once you confirm PrivateLink and provide allowlist details, we’ll draft a short network runbook and propose three 1-hour time slots for NetOps pairing.
- We’ll also produce a brief estimate for Dedicated vs Private deployment sizing for your expected throughput.

If it helps, I can loop in Marissa (solutions lead) and Vanessa (networking SLA owner) to handle IP and packet-level details.

Best,
Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: network-intake-form.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: redwood-privatelink-architecture.png (png)]

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@netfin.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@netfin.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 18:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Privatenet deployment screening — PrivateLink preference & IP allowlist next steps

Thanks, Nikhil — quick answers below.

1) PrivateLink is our preference. Our security team does not allow cross-account peering for third-party SaaS that handles customer data.
2) For the pilot we need a set of static egress IPs your service will use when making outbound calls (to our internal analytics and telemetry APIs). We cannot allow an open dynamic range. If PrivateLink is used inbound, we will also need the ENI IP(s) or NLB addresses that will terminate inside our subnet so we can add them to security groups.
3) NetOps lead: Tom Reed (tom.reed@netfin.com), he’s available for pairing on Tue/Wed mornings next week PST.
4) Procurement: we run on 30-day PO cycles; if you need a signed SOW for Dedicated capacity pricing, procurement@netfin.com is cc’d.

Attached is our information-security pre-screen (short questionnaire) — please return with answers to the network questions.

A couple of clarifying questions: can Redwood provide (a) a small list of static egress IPs for pilot and (b) an expected bandwidth/connection profile for the PrivateLink ENI? That will help our cloud team size firewall rules.

Best,
Alicia
Director, Cloud Operations
NetFin Corporation
[Attachment: netfin-sec-pre-screen.pdf (pdf)]

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@netfin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Privatenet deployment screening — PrivateLink preference & IP allowlist next steps

Appreciate the clarity, Alicia — forwarding answers and next-step plan below.

Short answers to your asks:
- We can support PrivateLink for inbound. For the pilot we can provision a stable set of 3 outbound egress IPs (NATed) that will be used by the Redwood-managed control plane for analytics/telemetry egress; these are static at the ASN level for the duration of the pilot.
- For the PrivateLink termination inside your VPC we typically provide the NLB hostname and the set of NLB IPs once the endpoint is provisioned; during the pilot we’ll share the ENI/NLB IPs as soon as they’re allocated.
- Bandwidth/profile: pilot expected at ~2000 tokens/s peak (estimate we discussed) — roughly translates to bursty HTTP requests around 50–120 Mbps total; we’ll formalize after we baseline with a short load test during the pairing session.

Next steps (proposed):
1) NetFin NetOps pairing (30–45m) — propose Tue 11/10 10:30am PST or Wed 11/11 9:30am PST. Please confirm Tom’s preferred slot.
2) NetFin to return the filled network-intake-form.pdf and the security pre-screen; we’ll map questions to configuration steps and share a one-page runbook.
3) We’ll produce a Pilot SOW addendum (networking appendix + IP commitments) for procurement.

I’ve attached a short implementation checklist we use for PrivateLink pilots — that covers who owns security group rules, expected time to provision, and signoff gates.

If you want the Dedicated sizing/estimate in parallel, let me know the 90th percentile expected RPS and average sequence length and we’ll run a quick cost delta for Dedicated vs Private.

Regards,
Nikhil
[Attachment: privatenet-implementation-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]

Internal notes / recommended answers for NetFin: 
- Egress IPs: commit to 3 static NAT IPs for pilot; operations will publish these in the runbook and keep them reserved. Add a 30-day notice for change.
- PrivateLink NLB: ops will supply NLB DNS + IPs post-provision (we should include a short TTL note).
- Load test: suggest we prepare a 15m load script that simulates 2k tokens/s and a second with a 5x burst; Marissa/Ben to own.
- Security artifacts: attach SOC 2 summary and our data-flow diagram (redwood-privatelink-architecture.png).
- Procurement: supply a short SOW appendix with a networking appendix and a separate cost line for Dedicated sizing if they request.

Action items for Nikhil:
- Lock the NetOps slot and confirm Tom’s calendar.
- Publish egress IP list once ops reserve.
- Draft the networking appendix for the Pilot SOW.

Marissa
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
